hens_rule_text: up to 4 fowl (hens) allowed on any residential premises; more than 4 requires a special permit; no roosters
permit_notes: No permit is needed for 4 or fewer fowl. Keeping more than 4 requires a special permit from the city.
setback_notes: Fowl pens, coops or runs must be at least 30 ft from any residence other than the keeper's own; sources describing a special-permit case for more than 4 fowl mention stricter distance rules (around 100 ft) but the exact text for that case was not confirmed.
coop_rules: Fowl and their housing must be kept away from neighboring residences per the 30 ft setback; no further coop construction standard confirmed.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Santa Ana Municipal Code Chapter 5 (Animals), Article I; roosters are separately banned citywide on residential premises under Sec. 5-6.5.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Search-result extracts quoted the actual code language (4-fowl limit, 30 ft setback, Sec. 5-6.5 rooster ban) from an elaws.us mirror of the Santa Ana code, but the full page could not be opened directly and the exact numbered section for the fowl-count rule (likely Sec. 5-6) was not fully confirmed; a secondary claim of a 100 ft rule for permitted flocks over 4 birds is noted but unverified.
